correctness.rationale: Every graph edge is an axiom instance, so reachability implies derivability. For the converse, predecessor sets E_r satisfy E_a subset E_b iff a reaches b. The operation f(E_r)=E_{r+1}, f(top)=top, and f(X)=empty otherwise is well-defined because mutual reachability is preserved by shifting paths. Positive exponents ensure every generating inequality f^n(X) subset f^m(X) holds for all subsets. Assigning p=E_0 therefore separates every non-reachable pair. No finite computation is used in the proof.

value.rationale: The result turns joint reasoning with any collection of positive modal reductions into an exact graph reachability problem and, more importantly, gives a complete redundancy/independence test with explicit countermodels. This is a structural closure theorem for a natural fragment generated by the reduction principles now studied in pure and normal modal logic, rather than a parameter census or routine recomputation.
